ch42.d.iso: Kind of decaying nucleus; the time unit follows its half-life
ch42.d.N0: Number of undecayed nuclei at the start
ch42.goal.random: Each nucleus decays independently and at random: probability $\lambda\,dt$ in a short time $dt$, whatever its age
ch42.goal.half: Many nuclei together follow $N(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$ and halve every half-life $T_{1/2}$
ch42.obs.single: Which nucleus decays when cannot be predicted (dots switch off at random on the grid; orange = just decayed)
ch42.obs.half: At $T_{1/2}$, $2T_{1/2}$, $3T_{1/2}$ about $N_0/2$, $N_0/4$, $N_0/8$ are left: however many remain, half of them decay in the next half-life
ch42.obs.small: $N_0 = 10$: big steps that stray far from the exponential, and every run differs
ch42.obs.large: $N_0 = 10000$: the steps almost vanish and the count lies on the exponential (relative fluctuation $\sim 1/\sqrt N$)
ch42.obs.iso: Changing the isotope only changes the time unit; the curve has the same shape (identical in $t/T_{1/2}$)
ch42.assume.indep: Nuclei do not affect each other; the decay probability per unit time is constant
ch42.assume.daughter: Daughter nuclei are taken as stable (²³⁸U's daughter ²³⁴Th actually decays further)
